title: Majestic Genius Draw
summary: Use promotion threats to gain king tempi before entering the opposing pawn’s square.

nodes.question: Can moving toward the corner help stop a distant pawn?
nodes.explanation: White has Kd8/a5 against Kd6/h7. Going straight toward h7 is too slow, but threatening a6 forces Black’s king to spend time on the a-file.

branches.title: Threaten promotion before racing home
commentary: Begin from the complete four-piece source root. The king retreats to create threats before returning toward the h-pawn; the final direct pawn race is an independently checked representative completion.
Kc8 threatens a6, after which Kc8 controls b7 and interferes with Black’s route to the pawn.
Kc6 approaches the a-pawn and meets that immediate threat.
Kb8 renews White’s promotion threat while preserving a way back toward the center.
Kb5 reaches the pawn, but spends another king tempo doing so.
Kb7 threatens to support the a-pawn again instead of rushing toward h7 immediately.
Kxa5 accepts the pawn and spends one more tempo away from the h-pawn.
Kc6 now reaches the drawing route. The three promotion threats have bought the necessary time.
h5 uses Black’s available double pawn move in the representative race.
Kd5 heads diagonally toward h1, remaining in the pawn’s square.
h4 advances toward promotion.
Ke4 keeps closing the distance.
h3 brings Black two steps from promotion.
Kf3 approaches g2.
h2 threatens to promote next move.
Kg2 reaches the capture square in time.
h1=Q+ promotes with check, but the new queen is undefended.
Kxh1 captures the queen. Only two kings remain, so the board position is drawn.

branches.title: Run toward the pawn immediately
commentary: Compare an independent direct king approach without first creating pawn threats.
Ke8 gives away the draw: Black need not spend any king moves dealing with a6.
h5 uses the initial double advance. The exact position is a Black win because White’s king is too far away and the a-pawn can be stopped.

branches.title: Push the a-pawn before improving the king
commentary: Compare the source’s premature pawn push.
a6 gives up the drawing tempo mechanism.
Kc6 approaches the pawn without being kept from b7.
a7 advances to the seventh rank, but the king cannot protect it.
Kb7 attacks a7 and stops promotion.
Ke7 moves White’s king away in the illustrated losing comparison.
h5 starts the distant passer while Kb7 keeps the a7 pawn blocked. The exact position remains winning for Black; taking a7 immediately instead would allow a draw.

branches.title: Black captures the a-pawn too early
commentary: Compare an independently checked early king capture in the losing-pawn-push variation.
a6 gives away White’s original draw.
Kc6 approaches the a-pawn.
a7 advances but cannot promote safely.
Kb7 blocks the pawn and preserves Black’s win.
Ke7 moves toward the distant h-pawn.
Kxa7 spends a tempo too far away: the exact remaining king-and-pawn ending is drawn. Black should start its pawn race while keeping a7 blocked instead.

exercises.prompt: Why not head straight toward h7?
exercises.answer: White first threatens promotion to make Black spend tempi on the a-pawn. Those forced responses let the king return to c6 in time to stop the h-pawn.
